name: Church Street Marketplace
note: Four blocks of Church Street, car-free and paved in brick since 1981. Buskers in summer, holiday lights in winter, and the place everyone ends up.

name: Ben & Jerry's first scoop shop
note: Ben Cohen and Jerry Greenfield opened their first ice cream shop on this corner in 1978, in an old gas station. The building is gone; a plaque marks the spot.

name: City Hall Park
note: Downtown's town green, in front of City Hall. Its fountain, lawn and benches fill up on the first warm day of spring.

name: The Flynn
note: An Art Deco movie palace from 1930, now Burlington's main stage for concerts, comedy and the jazz festival.

name: Battery Park
note: Named for the gun battery that fired on British ships in the War of 1812. Today it is where people go to watch the sun set behind the Adirondacks.

name: Waterfront and the bike path
note: The bike path runs along the lake from Oakledge to the Winooski River and on across the Colchester causeway, where a little bike ferry crosses the gap in summer.

name: ECHO
note: The science centre and aquarium for Lake Champlain, right on the water.

name: Ferry to Port Kent
note: In summer, the ferry from the King Street dock crosses Lake Champlain to Port Kent, New York, in about an hour.

name: Union Station
note: The 1916 station at the bottom of Main Street. Passenger trains came back in 2022, when Amtrak's Ethan Allen Express started running to New York City.

name: The breakwater lights
note: Two small lighthouses mark the ends of the breakwater that shelters the harbour.

name: UVM and Ira Allen Chapel
note: The University of Vermont was chartered in 1791. The chapel's tower, named for founder Ira Allen, is the landmark you see on the hill from the lake.

name: Pine Street and the South End
note: Old industrial buildings full of studios, breweries and makers. Every September the South End Art Hop opens them all up.

name: Oakledge Park
note: Rocky shoreline, swimming coves, and a treehouse built so wheelchairs can roll right up into it.

name: North Beach
note: The city's long sandy beach, with a campground in the pines behind it.

name: The Intervale
note: Farmland on the Winooski River's floodplain, a few minutes' bike ride from downtown. Working farms, community gardens and trails, all within the city.

name: Ethan Allen Homestead
note: The 1787 farmhouse where Ethan Allen, leader of the Green Mountain Boys, spent his last years.

name: Winooski Falls and the mills
note: The river drops over these falls, which once powered Winooski's big woollen mills. The mills are now shops, offices and apartments.

name: The Winooski roundabout
note: Downtown Winooski wraps around one big roundabout, with restaurants on every side of it.

name: Red Rocks Park
note: South Burlington's lakeside woods, with trails along reddish rock cliffs above the water.

name: Burlington airport
note: BTV, in South Burlington. Also home to the Vermont Air National Guard's F-35s, which you will hear before you see.
